description: Playable browser Minecraft-like named CUBELAND. Vite + TypeScript. YouTube-quality game slice, not a rotating cube.

userStories.title: Vite app with main.ts actually imported
userStories.description: player.ts is FIXED — never emit it again. Three tsc errors remain, all cross-file consistency: (1) src/main.ts uses the atlas as an object with properties tex/prog/buff/aP but src/atlas.ts exports a function (t:number)=>void — pick ONE shape: make atlas.ts export const atlas = { tex, prog, buff, aP, tick(t){...} } and keep main.ts as-is. (2) src/inventory.ts references B.STICK — add STICK to the block table in src/blocks.ts with the next free id. (3) src/blocks.ts line ~173 compares a tool kind (pick|axe) with a material (wood|stone) — compare tool kinds to tool kinds. Emit ONLY the files you change, each COMPLETE. The verify is npx tsc --noEmit.
userStories.verify: test -f src/main.ts && grep -q '/src/main.ts' index.html && grep -q '__CUBELAND_READY__' src/main.ts && npm install && npx tsc --noEmit

userStories.title: World + player render loop
userStories.description: STAGE 2: blocks.ts is DONE — never emit it again. Emit EXACTLY ONE file: src/world.ts, complete. Fix its two type errors and change nothing else structurally: (1) line ~210 calls this.buildMesh(...) but class World has no buildMesh — use the mesh-building method the class actually defines, or define buildMesh properly; make the name consistent. (2) line ~301 iterates a plain number with for..of — iterate the intended array/range instead. Keep the mesa terrain generation exactly as designed. File must be complete — if too long, trim comments, not logic.
acceptanceCriteria: World and Player constructed from main.ts
userStories.verify: npx tsc --noEmit && grep -q '__CUBELAND_READY__' src/main.ts && grep -R -q -E 'pointerlock|requestPointerLock|mousemove' src && grep -R -q -E 'WASD|KeyW|movement' src

userStories.title: Break and place blocks
userStories.description: Hold to break the targeted block. Right-click places the selected hotbar block. Hotbar keys 1-9. Visible hotbar UI with selected slot. Breaking takes time and shows a crack or progress. HARD RULES: do NOT emit index.html — build all hotbar/HUD UI from TypeScript DOM creation in a new src/hud.ts (DUSK style per the brief: skewed plum slots, orange selected border). Emit only files you change, each complete. blocks.ts and inventory.ts are frozen — use their existing exports.
userStories.verify: npx tsc --noEmit && grep -R -q -E 'break|mine|destroy' src && grep -R -q -E 'place|setBlock' src && grep -R -q -E 'hotbar|Digit1' src

userStories.title: Inventory + crafting table recipes
userStories.description: E toggles inventory. Crafting table recipes for planks, sticks, table, pickaxe/axe/shovel, torch. Inventory is a real grid, not an alert().

userStories.title: Day/night + one hostile
